title: Auto-cutover advisor: batching-aware cost thresholds, passive shadow validation, and staged rollback choreography
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Config cutovers (batching, KV cache settings, traffic routing) can create transient cost spikes or latency regressions that are non-obvious until after rollout. We need an automated advisor that layers cost-aware thresholds onto deploys, validates candidate config changes passively against live traffic, and coordinates a staged rollback choreography when safety signals trigger.

Goals:
- Surface batching/caching config changes that could increase unit cost (per-token) due to distribution shifts (shorter sequences => smaller batch packing, higher per-token GPU overhead).
- Run passive shadow validation for candidate config sets (duplicate requests evaluated without affecting responses) to gather realistic latency, token-efficiency, and cache-hit metrics pre-cutover.
- Define programmable rollback triggers (cost delta, p99 latency, KV-cache-miss-rate, model-quality regression via eval set) and guardrails that can be tuned per-customer and per-deployment tier.
- Implement a staged rollback choreography: safe pause -> incremental traffic drain -> config revert -> state reconciliation (idempotent snapshot replay of KV cache / prewarm) -> health-verification.

Acceptance criteria:
- Advisor recommends a batching/caching profile change or blocks auto-apply when projected >10% unit cost increase for a given traffic slice.
- Shadow validation produces a 95th percentile confidence interval for p99 latency, token-efficiency, and cache-hit delta within 1 hour of sampling for 95% of test runs.
- Rollback triggers execute within 30s of threshold breach and complete reversible cutover with <2% request error increase and <5% traffic loss during transition in Core infra tests.
- New telemetry pipelines (advisor-run-id tagged) feed rollback audits into Console so SRE/PM can review post-mortem.

Design notes / approach:
- Cost projection: combine model of batching distribution (observed seq-length histogram) with runtime kernel cost curve (tokens-per-second per-batch-size) to estimate unit cost delta for candidate config.
- Shadow validation: fork requests into an isolated runner that records latency, kv-hit/miss, and token count without adding to user-visible token billing. Runs for configurable sample ratio (default 1%).
- Triggers: configurable rule engine with rate-limit hysteresis to avoid flapping (eg. require breach for 3/5 windows). Support both absolute and relative thresholds.
- State reconciliation: capture idempotent snapshot of service-level state (cache keys, prewarm seeds) before cutover; when rollback occurs, apply snapshot with backoff and verify by replaying synthetic prefix workload to rehydrate caches.
- Safety-first rollout: default staged ramp (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic pause if any trigger breaches.

Implementation plan:
1) Low-risk prototype: implement cost projection service and a Console recommendation panel (read-only), 1 sprint.
2) Shadow runner: integrate lightweight request fork and metrics capture, 2 sprints.
3) Rollout rule engine + rollback choreography orchestrator, 2 sprints.
4) E2E tests and canary on Dedicated environment, 1 sprint.

Open trade-offs:
- Sampling ratio for shadow validation: higher gives stronger signal but more infra cost. Plan to default to 1% with customer-override.
- Snapshot granularity: full KV snapshot vs. prefix-only for affected model variants. Start with prefix-only to limit storage and replay time.
- Tightness of cost delta threshold: 10% is our initial guardrail; we'll tune with customer experiments.
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem on config cutover that caused a transient 18% unit-cost bump for payments flow. Attached initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COST/Auto-cutover+Advisor

2026-02-17 Marco Ruiz: Spike complete for cost-projection math. Found that small shifts in seq-length distribution (median -15 tokens) can increase per-token GPU overhead by ~6% under current kernel selection. Recorded notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1XbCostSpike

2026-02-24 Design review (Leah Chen): UX recommended making 'shadow validation' opt-in at first for customer privacy and billing clarity. Also asked for a compact visualization of batch-distribution projections in Console.

2026-03-03 Eng sync: Implemented initial cost model and Console panel prototype. PR# https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 (draft). Performance microbench harness added under /bench/auto-cutover. Unit tests passing locally.

2026-03-09 QA: Integration tests revealed flapping when transient GC pauses cause p99 to spike briefly; added hysteresis: trigger must be true in 3 of 5 consecutive 1-min windows before rollback. See test log: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/2859

2026-03-12 Marco Ruiz: Shadow runner beta deployed to Dedicated staging for Payments team. Observed a KV cache miss rate increase on candidate config for small-seq traffic slice (miss delta +12%). Recommended prefix-only snapshot and prewarm on rollback path; implementing in next PR.
